artifact.summary: Measurement-free unitary for n iterations of a qubit-probe weak measurement on one system qubit. Each iteration applies a system pulse U_k, then exp(-i*eps_k*H_SP) with an assumed constant H_SP = |1><1|_S (x) X_P, implemented as a controlled-RX(2*eps_k) onto a fresh probe qubit. Probes start in |0> (prepared by the runner) and are read out in the computational basis by the runner. Projecting probe k onto <j| gives K_0 = diag(1, cos eps), K_1 = diag(0, -i sin eps), which have distinct singular values.
register_layout: qubit 0: system S (computational basis, qubit 0 is least significant bit)
qubit k+1: probe P_k (iteration k+1), expected input |0>; up to 11 probes

equation_mapping.explanation: Completeness of the Kraus operators follows from the global unitarity of the circuit (a probe-outcome partition) and is not coded separately.
Unitary exp(-i eps H_SP) with the assumed H_SP = |1><1|_S (x) X_P, acting on a fresh probe. The projection onto <j|_P (probe measurement) is left to the runner.

equation_mapping.code_location: build_circuit: loop over k with qc.u(...) then qc.crx(...)
equation_mapping.explanation: Interleaves system pulses U_k with weak-interaction iterations, using one fresh probe per iteration so that the Kraus product K_{j_n}U_n...K_{j_1}U_1 arises after probe outcomes are read. Coarse-graining is not implemented.

The SVD and distinct-singular-value condition is a characterization of achievable measurements, not an operation. The chosen H_SP gives K_0 = diag(1, cos eps), which has distinct singular values, but nothing checks that.

specification_changes.change: Chose the specific constant Hamiltonian H_SP = |1><1|_S (x) X_P, with initial probe |0> and computational-basis readout.
specification_changes.reason: The abstract and spec leave H_SP unspecified, and a concrete choice is needed. A Z(x)X-type coupling would give two Kraus operators with equal singular values, so it was avoided.

specification_changes.change: Scope narrowed to a fixed, user-given list of iteration strengths and pulse angles, with no feedback, stopping rule or coarse-graining. Pulses are U3 gates (U(2), differing from SU(2) by a global phase). Probe measurements are deferred, and fresh probe qubits are used instead of reset.
specification_changes.reason: The feedback rule is unspecified and dynamic circuits, reset and measurement are disallowed. Fresh probes make the circuit a unitary on the system plus the probes.
They are a background constraint and a characterization result, respectively.

assumptions: The system is a single qubit.
The probe starts in |0> and is prepared by the runner.
Probe readout is in the computational basis and is done by the runner.
H_SP = |1><1|_S (x) X_P, so exp(-i eps H_SP) is a controlled-RX with angle 2*eps.
Fixed pulse angles and a fixed number of iterations are supplied in the instance.
If pulses are omitted, identity pulses are used.
unresolved_issues: The paper's actual interaction Hamiltonian is unknown.
The feedback rule, stopping criterion and outcome coarse-graining to M_0 and M_1 are not implemented.
The continuous-time limit and the characterization theorem are not reconstructed.
The number of iterations is capped at 11 by the 12-qubit limit, which is far from a continuous decomposition.

validation.detail: Circuit built and transpiled successfully; no independent correctness reference selected.
